title: SELinux Denial Monitoring
exclusions: Does not replace enterprise SIEM correlation for unrelated threat classes. Does not constitute legal, regulatory, or executive attestation for 'SELinux Denial Monitoring'. Does not cover entities explicitly scoped out in operational_exceptions.csv. Pair with sibling UCs in the same subcategory when the SPL surface alone cannot prove control effectiveness (see prerequisiteUseCases on UC-1.1.66).
evidence: Saved search uc_1_1_66_selinux_denial_monitoring, dashboard panel tied to this UC, weekly CSV export archived to index=evidence with change-ticket reference, and git-tracked lookup baselines referenced in the search.

controlTest.positiveScenario: On a lab host or staging index, ingest sample events that satisfy all SPL filters for 'SELinux Denial Monitoring'. Run the saved search manually and confirm at least one result row with populated severity or metric fields. Verify the alert action fires within one schedule interval and the output matches the dashboard table projection for UC-1.1.66.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest a control batch where threshold fields remain within normal bounds (for example compliant configuration values, timestamps outside the monitoring window, or entities listed in operational_exceptions.csv). Confirm the saved search returns zero rows, no notable is created, and scheduled export volume to the evidence index stays flat.

dataSources: `sourcetype=syslog` (or `linux_audit`) carrying SELinux **denied** lines Collected via Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: `Splunk_TA_nix` — Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833)
spl:
index=os sourcetype=syslog (SELinux OR setroubleshoot) denied
| stats count by host, source_context, target_context, object
| where count>5
description: Groups SELinux **denied** log lines by subject/object context so you can see where policy blocks cluster and whether a single tuple suddenly spikes.
value: Policy mistakes and real attacks both show up as **deny** first; a grouped view is faster for app owners to tune booleans and for security to see lateral movement in **context** space.
implementation: If you already ingest **linux_audit** with structured fields, switch the first line to that sourcetype; syslog-only shops should ensure **setroubleshootd** or **auditd** lines actually reach the **os** index. Parse **object** if your build leaves it in `_raw` only.

references.title: Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled maintenance windows** — Planned change activity in the CMDB or change calendar produces expected deviations that match this detection pattern during approved maintenance. Cross-check ServiceNow change records for `state=implement` and the affected CI list.

2. **Backup and batch job cycles** — Nightly ETL, backup agents, or log rotation jobs generate bursts of similar events that resemble alert conditions but occur on a fixed schedule. Compare `_time` against the documented batch window before paging.

3. **Onboarding and provisioning bursts** — New users, devices, or services provisioned in bulk can temporarily skew counts until baselines stabilize. Filter events tagged `onboarding=true` in the identity or asset lookup.

4. **Monitoring and health-check traffic** — Synthetic transactions or internal scanner accounts generate probe traffic designed to exercise the control. Exclude service accounts listed in `monitoring_exceptions.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** Maintain a KV Store lookup `operational_exceptions.csv` with columns `entity`, `exception_reason`, `valid_from`, `valid_until`, and `approved_by`. Join the saved search to this lookup and filter `where isnull(exception_reason) OR now() > valid_until` so approved windows suppress alerts without muting the search globally.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Kernel **audit** and SELinux in **enforcing** mode with logging you can read from `/var/log/audit/audit.log` and/or `journalctl` with **SELinux** tags.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
**Props** for **source_context** / **target_context** (or the AVC string equivalents) are critical; use the TA’s add-on for Linux props where possible.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
`action` in `stats` is removed because many builds never extracted it—re-add when your parser supplies it. Start as a **report**; alert after two consecutive windows `>5` for the same tuple.

**CIM** — There is no clean **All_Traffic**-style field for an AVC; keep this on raw unless you also model it into a custom data model.


Step 3 — Validate
`ausearch -m avc` on the host for the same second as Splunk; `sealert` (setroubleshoot) for human-readable text if you use the GUI helper.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Send **deny** spikes to the app that owns the **target** context, not only SOC, when the pattern matches a release.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk_TA_nix` — Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=syslog into os. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`host, object, source_context, target_context`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: We help you see when the “extra safety wrapper” on the system keeps saying no, often for the same file or the same app role, so people can fix policy or look for mischief.
